title: Reductive group-scheme structure of PGL
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $r\geq1$. The group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] $H=\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}=\operatorname{GL}_{r,k}/\mathbf G_{m,k}$, the fppf sheaf quotient of invertible matrices by scalar matrices, is a smooth affine group scheme of finite type over $k$, is geometrically connected, and has trivial geometric unipotent radical. Here reductive means smooth, affine and of finite type with geometrically connected fibres and with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup after algebraic closure; unipotent means that in a faithful matrix representation every geometric point is a unipotent matrix. The fppf quotient means the sheafification of $R\mapsto\operatorname{GL}_r(R)/R^\times$ for faithfully flat finitely presented covers of $k$-algebras. For $r=1$ this is the trivial group scheme.

source.place: Example 5.49, Example 19.19 and Corollary 17.62(d); central quotient of GL_r by its scalar radical, including r=1.

proof.text: First treat $r=1$. The functor of points in [def-sc-general-linear-group] gives $\operatorname{GL}_{1,k}(A)=A^\times$ with its scalar subgroup equal to the entire group, namely $\mathbf G_m$ of [def-sc-gm-ga]. Thus the quotient presheaf has one element on every $k$-algebra and its sheafification is the terminal sheaf, represented by $\operatorname{Spec}k$ with the trivial group law. Its structure morphism is the identity, so it is smooth, affine, of finite type, geometrically connected, and has no nontrivial subgroup. This proves all clauses for $r=1$. In the remaining steps assume $r\geq2$.

Use [lem-sfb-projective-matrix-central-cover] for $r\geq2$. It gives the affine group scheme $H$, its faithfully flat scalar $\mathbf G_m$-torsor $\operatorname{GL}_{r,k}\to H$, smoothness, finite type and geometric connectedness, all compatible with field extension. Its stated quotient is the fpqc sheaf quotient. To check the fppf quotient convention of the item, use [lem-sfb-projective-frames-pgl] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the free rank-$r$ bundle: the same projective invertible-matrix classes lift Zariski locally to matrices, and two lifts differ exactly by a scalar unit. The fpqc quotient is already an fppf sheaf. The natural map from the presheaf $A\mapsto\operatorname{GL}_r(A)/A^\times$ into it is injective: if two global matrices become scalar multiples Zariski locally, their scalar units agree on overlaps (multiply by the inverse matrix), hence glue to a unit of $A$. Every section is locally in its image for a Zariski covering, hence for an fppf covering. Indeed choose the local matrix lifts; their classes agree on overlaps by the scalar criterion, and they glue uniquely in the quotient sheaf. Thus the induced map from the fppf sheafification is an isomorphism, with the same group law. This identifies the sheaf named in the item with $H$ and proves its geometric clauses except reductivity.

source.place: Example 5.49 and Propositions 5.24--5.27, printed pp.104--105,111; the Zariski-local scalar quotient is expanded via the existing projective-frame node.

proof.text: Put $G=\operatorname{GL}_{r,k}$. By [lem-sfb-general-linear-reductive], $G$ is reductive over the original field $k$: the conclusion concerns its geometric unipotent radical, so it applies even if $k$ is imperfect. Its smoothness, affineness, finite type and geometric connectedness are also part of that statement. These are exactly the hypotheses needed for the reductive-radical theorem used below.

Compute the scheme-theoretic centre of $G$ using the invertible-matrix functor of [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Fix a commutative $k$-algebra $A$. A central $A$-point must commute with every matrix after every $A$-algebra extension; in particular, over $A$ it commutes with $I+E_{ij}$ for each $i
e j$. This transvection has inverse $I-E_{ij}$, and subtracting $M$ from the commuting identity gives $ME_{ij}=E_{ij}M$. Entrywise the equality is $M_{ai}\delta_{jb}=\delta_{ai}M_{jb}$ for all $a,b$, where $\delta$ is $1$ for equal indices and $0$ otherwise. Taking $b=j$ and $a
e i$ gives $M_{ai}=0$; taking $(a,b)=(i,j)$ gives $M_{ii}=M_{jj}$. No cancellation of a nonunit or division by an integer occurs. For each column $i$ choose $j
e i$, possible because $r\geq2$; hence all off-diagonal entries vanish, and varying the pair makes all diagonal entries equal. Thus $M=aI$. From $MM^{-1}=I$ we obtain $a(M^{-1})_{11}=1$, so $a$ is a unit. Conversely, every scalar unit commutes with every invertible matrix over every $A$-algebra. The two assignments $a\mapsto aI$ and $M\mapsto M_{11}$ are inverse group maps, and entrywise application of any $k$-algebra homomorphism commutes with both. They therefore identify the scheme-theoretic centre functor with the scalar $\mathbf G_m$ of [def-sc-gm-ga], including on nonreduced algebras. This centre is already a torus: the one-factor split multiplicative group.

source.place: Example 12.47, printed p.246: centre of GL is Gm; explicit transvection calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-radical-quotient] to the reductive $G$ from step 3. Its radical $R(G)$ is the largest torus in $Z(G)$. Step 4 identifies $Z(G)$ itself with the scalar torus, hence $R(G)=\mathbf G_m$. The theorem says that the fppf sheaf quotient $G/R(G)$ is reductive and semisimple. Step 2 identifies this quotient with $H$. To spell out the geometric assertion, choose an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$. The base-field clause of the radical theorem gives $R(G_{\bar k})=R(G)_{\bar k}=\mathbf G_{m,\bar k}$, and the field-extension compatibility in step 2 identifies $H_{\bar k}$ with $G_{\bar k}/\mathbf G_{m,\bar k}$. Thus the semisimple quotient in the theorem is precisely $H_{\bar k}$: it has no nontrivial smooth connected normal solvable closed subgroup scheme, and in particular no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup scheme, as the theorem explicitly states. This proves the remaining geometric-unipotent-radical clause without a perfectness assumption on $k$. Together with steps 1 and 2 it proves all clauses for every $r\geq1$.

source.place: Corollary 17.62(b)--(d), printed pp.372--373, applied after Example 19.19 and the scalar-centre calculation.

Live and side-live still show the item unsplit with an empty proof, neither child exists there, and there is no repair note. Both new nodes (lem-sfb-general-linear-reductive, lem-sfb-reductive-radical-quotient) are byte-identical to 38b3. In the item, the statement, stmt_deps, source, proof_deps and step uses are unchanged; only the step-4 text and one split_report sentence changed. The cited central-cover and projective-frames-pgl nodes are byte-identical to 38b3. I re-read def-sc-general-linear-group (R-points are the invertible matrices), def-sc-gm-ga, def-sc-group-scheme and def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup. Steps: (1) For r=1, GL_1 equals its scalar subgroup, so the quotient is Spec k. (2) Zariski-local lifts plus gluing of scalar units identify the fppf quotient with the fpqc PGL_r for r>=2. (3) GL_r is reductive by Milne iAG2017 Ex 19.19 with Cor 19.18 (p.401), re-read in the text. (4) The new identity (ME_ij)_{ab}=M_{ai}delta_{jb}=delta_{ai}M_{jb}=(E_ij M)_{ab} is correct. b=j with a!=i gives M_ai=0, and (a,b)=(i,j) gives M_ii=M_jj. A j!=i exists since r>=2. No division is used, so the step holds in every characteristic and over nonreduced A, and the inverse maps a->aI and M->M_11 are natural. (5) Milne Cor 17.62(b)-(d), re-read on pp.372-373, gives R(G)=Z(G)_t=G_m and R(G_kbar)=R(G)_kbar. The central-cover field-extension clause gives H_kbar=G_kbar/G_m, which is semisimple and so has no smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup; k need not be perfect. Edge cases checked: a torus, the trivial group, SL_p in characteristic p with Z=mu_p, GL_1=G_m. Neither child restates an item clause, there is no cycle, no SGA is cited and there are no tool_uses. No changes. Maintainer note: this is a promotion loop with the same mathematics as the four earlier PASSes.
